docs.title: Upload Basemap Overlay Layer
docs.text: This workflow allows you to upload a GeoTIFF file into the system to serve as either a basemap or an overlay layer in the map viewer. You will be guided through selecting the layer type, uploading the file, configuring its display settings (like name, sorting, and icon), assigning visibility permissions, and finally previewing the result on a map.

docs.title: Step 1: Select Layer Type
docs.text:
The first step requires you to choose what type of layer you are creating.

  • Make a Selection: You will see a grid of option cards. Click on the card that represents the type of map layer you wish to process (e.g., Basemap or Overlay).
  • Confirmation: The selected card will highlight with a blue border and a light blue background to indicate it is active.

[IMAGE PLACEHOLDER: Step 1 Process Selection] Highlight suggestion: Draw a box around the active/selected card showing the blue border and background.

docs.title: Step 2: Upload GEOTIFF File & Settings
docs.text:
Once the layer type is selected, you will upload your spatial data and configure how it will appear in the system.

  • Upload the File: In the dashed dropzone area, either drag and drop your .tif / .tiff file or click the "Choose GEOTIFF file…" button.
  • Map Layer Name: Enter a clear, descriptive name for your layer in this required text field. This is how it will appear to users in the map viewer.
  • Sort Order: Enter a number to determine where this layer sits in the list of available map layers. (Note: The higher the number, the lower the layer will appear in the list).
  • Map Layer Icon: Select an icon to represent your layer. You can use the "Search icons..." bar to find a specific symbol (e.g., 'map' or 'globe') and select it from the grid below. The chosen icon will appear in the preview box next to the title.

[IMAGE PLACEHOLDER: Step 2 Upload and Settings] Highlight suggestion: Highlight the Dropzone area, the "Map Layer Name" input field, and the "Map Layer Icon" search and grid section.

docs.title: Step 3: Choose Basemap Visibility
docs.text:
After filling out the settings and clicking the submit button at the bottom of the form, a visibility modal will appear.

  • Set Access Level: Choose who can see this map layer by selecting one of the two options:
    • Public: Accessible to anyone on the internet.
    • Private: Only accessible to authorized, logged-in users.
  • Confirm: Once you have made your selection, click the blue "Confirm and Create" button to finalize the upload and create the layer.

[IMAGE PLACEHOLDER: Step 3 Visibility Modal] Highlight suggestion: Highlight the Public and Private option cards within the modal, and the "Confirm and Create" button.

docs.title: Step 4: Preview Your Layer
docs.text:
After the system successfully processes the GeoTIFF and creates the layer, you will be taken to a final summary screen.

  • Map Preview: You will see a map container displaying a preview of your newly uploaded layer, allowing you to visually verify that the geographic data has been placed and rendered correctly.

[IMAGE PLACEHOLDER: Step 4 Map Preview] Highlight suggestion: Draw a subtle border around the map preview container to show where the newly uploaded layer is rendered.

docs.title: GeoNode
docs.text:
GeoNode is the spatial data catalogue of Mare Nostrum LAB. It is a fork of GeoNode-Project used as the Spatial Data Repository on the platform.

The full upstream user guide is here.

This section only covers what Mare Nostrum LAB instance adds on top of that: the Mare Nostrum LAB plugin (thesaurus keywords and local coordinate systems).

To use the stock catalogue (upload a layer, set permissions, share a map), follow the official guide. The pages below describe the extra metadata widgets and CRS handling.

docs.title: MN Thesauri plugin
docs.text: This plugin is a dedicated GeoNode app. It adds Mare Nostrum LAB thesauri (and related keyword fields) to dataset metadata. Local coordinate systems are accepted on import and transformed to GeoNode’s default web CRS (EPSG:4326 and EPSG:3857).

docs.title: Open metadata editing
docs.text:
1. Open a dataset.

  2. In the top bar, open Edit and choose Edit Metadata.

docs.title: Thesauri fields on the form
docs.text:
The metadata form has extra sections next to the standard GeoNode fields. Each section title has an i icon; hover it for a short hint about what belongs in that field.

  • Mare Nostrum Lab Thesaurus — the project’s own vocabulary (the same Wikibase as Cradle and Recogito).
  • External Thesauri — Wikidata and World Historical Gazetteer. Assigned values look like Nea Pafos [Wd:Q22991943].

  • Data Format — technical format of the file (for example GeoTIFF). This list can also be opened with the dropdown arrow.

The field only shows values already assigned to the record:

  • selected values appear as blue tags,
  • the x on a tag removes that one value,
  • the x on the right of the field (before the arrow) clears the whole field,
  • the down arrow opens a short predefined list (used for Data Format),
  • Change (on the right of the field) opens the search window described below.

docs.title: Browse the thesauri
docs.text: Change button opens a popup to search the chosen vocabulary and add concepts. Each thesaurus field has its own Change button on the right.

docs.title: Empty search
docs.text:
The header Browse MN Thesaurus shows which dictionary you are querying. Close dismisses the window without applying a new selection.

  1. Type at least three characters in the search box (placeholder: Enter at least 3 characters or press Enter).

Add selected stays inactive until at least one result is checked.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
The list is scrollable. Each hit has a checkbox (you can pick several), a blue title link, and a short description (often description added automatically).

  1. Check one or more concepts.

  2. Press Add selected. The modal closes and the chosen items appear as blue tags on the form.

docs.title: Local coordinate systems
docs.text: This instance accepts datasets in local / site CRS. On import, geometries are transformed to GeoNode’s default systems, EPSG:4326 and EPSG:3857.

docs.title: Account Management
docs.text: This section provides information on logging in to the Thesaurus account and changing an account password.

docs.title: Logging in to the account
docs.text:
Login is required for some activities

Note that there are several actions (e.g., adding and editing contents) that require you to log in first.

  1. Find and select the "Log in" button at the top right corner or click here.

  2. Provide your "Username" and "Password" in dedicated fields and click the "Log in" button.

    Remain logged in

    Check the "Keep me logged in" option to remain logged in after closing the session.

    Password reset

    "Forgot your password?" option does not work due to the lack of an email protocol connection. For a password reset, please contact the Thesaurus administrator.

  3. After completing the procedure, you will be redirected to your user profile page. Moreover, in the top right corner, the user's login appears.

docs.title: Changing the password
docs.text:
1. Log in to the account.

  2. Go to the "Change Password" option on the Main page or click here.

  3. Enter your new password, retype it in the required field and press "Change credentials" button.

  4. Once changed, a confirmation page will be displayed.

docs.title: Appendices
docs.text:
In this section, you can find useful information about:

  • Thesaurus Management System Components

  • Division of Responsibilities Between Components

  • Key Terms and Definitions

  • Object Feature Storage Structure

  • Properties in Hierarchical Dictionaries

  • Inverse Properties

  • Important Design Decisions Regarding Data Modeling

docs.title: Thesaurus Management System Components
docs.text:
Dictionary management is provided through four complementary components (click to visit):

  1. Mare Nostrum LAB thesaurus - a dictionary database that stores individual terms organized into thematic categories in a structured format.

  2. Cradle - a tool for adding new dictionary entries to Mare Nostrum LAB thesaurus.

  3. Wikibase Query Service (WBQS) - a tool for advanced searching of Mare Nostrum LAB thesaurus using SPARQL queries.

  4. QuickStatements - a tool for batch editing and bulk importing data into Mare Nostrum LAB thesaurus.

docs.title: Division of Responsibilities Between Components
docs.text:
The table below presents a summary of the division of responsibilities for the tools described in the previous section.

Tool Responsibility Provided Features Mare Nostrum LAB thesaurus A dictionary database that stores data in Linked Data format as an advanced network of interconnections. - Browsing data- Displaying hierarchical data- Manually adding new dictionary values Cradle A visual graphical editor supporting the addition of new records to the dictionary database via an intuitive interface with a predefined set of required properties for a given thematic set. - Adding new dictionary values in accordance with the established data model- Adding hierarchically dependent dictionary values Wikibase Query Service An advanced tool for multi-level searching of the dictionary database. Usage requires knowledge of SPARQL syntax as well as the relationships and structures within the Wikidata Mare Nostrum database. - Browsing data- Thematic filtering of database content- Creating data visualizations QuickStatements A tool for batch editing and bulk importing data into the dictionary database. It allows executing sequence-based commands (CSV/V1 formats) to automate large-scale data modifications. - Bulk importing and creating new records- Batch adding, modifying, or removing statements and properties- Automated processing of structured datasets

docs.title: Key Terms and Definitions
docs.text:
Item - a thing, entity or concept. It can be an object, a person, an event, a location, a work of art, or an abstract concept. Items are designated by unique identifiers starting with the letter "Q" followed by a positive integer.

Label - the primary name of an item in a given language. It provides the essential information needed to identify the topic of the item. Labels do not have to be unique.

Description - a short phrase intended to disambiguate items that have identical or similar labels. While descriptions do not need to be unique on their own, two items cannot share both the same label and the same description.

Alias - an alternative name for the same item in a given language. It can be a synonym, colloquial name, abbreviation, or historical name. Aliases improve the searchability of items within the database.

docs.title: Object Feature Storage Structure
docs.text:
Data concerning items (Q) in Mare Nostrum LAB thesaurus is stored as triplets: item (Q) - property (P) - value, where:

  • Item - indicates the identifier of the entity it refers to.

  • Property - defines a relationship or feature of the given item. Each property has an assigned data type that dictates what values can be entered. The list of available properties in the Mare Nostrum LAB thesaurus project is available here.

  • Value - represents the actual data associated with the item (it can be another item (Q), a string, a date and time, or geographic point coordinates in the WGS84 system, among others).

Figure below presents a graphical example of the feature storage structure.

(blue rectangle - Item; arrows - Properties; green rectangles - Values)

Image source: Wikidata Query Service Tutorial

docs.title: Properties in Hierarchical Dictionaries
docs.text:
• subclass of (P2) - indicates that one object is a subclass or subset of another. It sould not be confused with instance of (P1).

    Example: A volcano is a subclass of mountain; Mount Everest is an instance of mountain.

  • part of (P20) - indicates that one item is an integral part of another. This property is mainly used in the provenance and chronology dictionaries.

Additional properties used in the dictionaries, but not displayed in the hierarchical structure:

  • modified version of (P18) - indicates that one object is a modified version of another, yet the second object cannot be unambiguously considered identical to the first.

  • said to be the same as (P17) - used when there is a need to add two independent items representing the same object under different names, provided the user does not want to declare the second entity as an alias of the first.

docs.title: Inverse Properties
docs.text:
When manually adding items, it is good practice to add an inverse relationship pointing from the parent item to the child item. Defining this connection is important for efficient navigation between item pages within the hierarchy.

Adding a new Item with Cradle

Cradle is configured to automatically add a specific inverse property of the declared property.

Example: If you are adding the item "beige", which is a subclass of (P2) "hierarchical color of the soil", you should also define the property superclass of (P11) "beige" for the "hierarchical color of the soil" item.

The table below presents the properties used in the Mare Nostrum LAB thesaurus dictionaries along with their inverses.

Property Inverse Occurrence subclass of (P2) superclass of (P11) all dictionaries excluding "provenance" and "chronology" modified version of (P18) has modification(s) (P19) mainly "sub-category" said to be the same as (P17) said to be the same as (P17) all dictionaries part of (P20) has part(s) (P21) "provenance" and "chronology"

docs.title: Important Design Decisions Regarding Data Modeling
docs.text:
1. Amphora Type, Vessel Form, Sub-category, Morphology, State of Preservation and Surface Treatment Dictionaries

    These dictionaries were modeled exclusively using subclass of (P2), where the parent item represents the dictionary itself and the child item represents a specific dictionary value.

  2. Vessel Part, Harris Matrix Relationships, Trench Parameters, Visual Item Metadata, Linguistic Object Metadata

    These dictionaries were modeled using subclass of (P2) as hierarchical structures. The parent item represents the dictionary, the first-level child item represents a general "family" of concepts (e.g., "lower part"), and the second-level child item represents a specific type (e.g., "base", "sherd").

    Note

    This approach does not exclude adding a standalone item without a "concept family" at the first child level (e.g., "almost complete").

  3. Provenance Dictionary

    This dictionary was modeled using part of (P20) on every level of "concept family" (e.g., "Asia Minor" is part of "provenance" and "Phocaea" is part of "Asia Minor").

  4. Chronology Dictionary

    This dictionary was modeled using part of (P20) similarly to point 3. However, it requires distinguishing between two conceptual meanings:

    • Parts within a single period (e.g., "ER I", "ER II", "ER III" as parts of "ER")
    • Parts of a period spanning two epochs (e.g., "ER" as part of "LH/ER").

    Both contexts use the same property (part of (P20)), though its semantic interpretation differs slightly.

    The figure below provides a graphical exaplanation of the terms used in this section to describe hierarchy nesting levels.

docs.title: Creating a New Record in the Thesaurus - Cradle
docs.text: Cradle is a form-based tool for adding new items to the Mare Nostrum LAB thesaurus dictionaries. Use it when you need to create a record in a specific dictionary (e.g., vessel part, provenance, etc.).

docs.title: Opening Cradle from the Main Page
docs.text:
1. Go to the Thesaurus Main Page.

  2. In the Dictionaries section, select a New [dictionary name] link (for example, New amphora type, New vessel part, etc.).

docs.title: Logging In and Authorizing the Tool
docs.text:
Cradle can only save new items after you log in and grant it permission to edit the Thesaurus.

  1. On the form page, click Log in to save! in the top-right corner.

  2. Sign in with your Mare Nostrum LAB thesaurus account.

    Account required

    If you are already logged in, you will not see the login page. If you do not have an account yet, follow the steps in Account Management.

  3. On the authorization page, click Allow to permit Cradle to make changes on your behalf.

After a successful authorization, the form for the selected dictionary becomes ready to fill in.

docs.title: Form Layout
docs.text:
Each Cradle form has the same core structure. Required fields are marked with a red asterisk (*).

  1. Labels (required) - the name of the new item in the selected language.
  2. Also known as (optional) - alternative names (aliases) in the selected language.
  3. Descriptions (recommended) - a short description in the selected language that distinguishes the item from similar ones.
  4. Subclass of/Part of (required) - the parent item that places the new record in the dictionary hierarchy.
  5. Additional properties - dictionary-specific fields. Whether they are required depends on the particular dictionary.

Important interface elements:

  • Language selector - a dropdown before each text field in Labels, Also known as, and Descriptions. Choose the appropriate language for the label, description, or alias you are entering.
  • Add (+) and remove (-) buttons - visible after each text field. Click + to add another entry in a different language (pick the language in the dropdown first); click − to remove an extra language entry.
  • Hover over the ⓘ icon next to a property to see its definition.
  • Click the Mare Nostrum logo in the top-right corner to return to the Main Page.
Language

Enter the primary label in English. To add labels, descriptions, or aliases in other languages, use the language selector and the + button next to the relevant field. Available languages: English (EN), Polish (PL), Greek (EL), German (DE), French (FR).

Example form showing described above elements and its dictionary-specific fields

docs.title: Filling In and Submitting the Form
docs.text:
1. Complete all required fields (marked with a red asterisk).
  2. Fill in optional fields as needed for the dictionary you are editing.

  3. When the required fields are complete, the Create new item button appears at the bottom of the form.

    Button not visible?

    If required fields are filled, but Create new item still does not appear, click anywhere outside the currently focused field to refresh the form state.

  4. Click Create new item.

  5. Wait while the page shows Creating item...

  6. When creation succeeds, the Last items created section appears with a link to the new item.

Open the link to review the new record and, if needed, continue editing it on the item page.

docs.title: Creating a Subtype of an Existing Item
docs.text:
By default, the subclass of/part of field points to the main parent of the dictionary. You can instead choose the new item under another existing dictionary entry.

For example: add example paphos as a subtype of paphos, rather than directly under amphora type.

  1. Open the Cradle form for the target dictionary.
  2. In the subclass of/part of field, replace the default parent with the existing item that should be the direct parent.

  3. Complete the remaining required fields and click Create new item.

docs.title: Mare Nostrum LAB thesaurus - Management
docs.text: This section is dedicated to explain all specific procedures which allow searching, modifying and deleting information from the Mare Nostrum LAB thesaurus.

docs.title: Available Data
docs.text:
The Mare Nostrum LAB thesaurus project offers the following data dictionaries (click to explore):

  • pottery types - amphorae - Mediterranean amphora types

  • pottery types - lamps - Mediterranean lamp types

  • pottery types - table ware - Mediterranean table ware types

  • pottery - morphology - geometric characteristics of fragments

  • pottery - vessel form - general morphological categories

  • pottery - vessel part - preserved component part of a vessel

  • pottery - sub-category - detailed product specification (primarily refers to the ceramic fabric/paste, which sometimes implies a specific repertoire of vessel types)

  • pottery - state of preservation - state of preservation of a found fragment

  • pottery - surface treatment - type of exterior wall finishing

  • provenance - hierarchical dictionary of vessel production sites

  • chronology - hierarchical timeframes

  • Harris matrix relationships - stratigraphic relationships according to the Harris matrix (describing chronological and spatial links between stratigraphic units)

  • trench parameters - parameters defining the physical, material, and methodological characteristics of an archaeological trench. This includes:

    • archaeological remains - types of recovered artifacts and materials

    • context characterization - physical properties of the excavated layer, including its origin, soil color, grain size, and soil density

    • excavation procedures - methods applied during the excavation of the trench

  • visual item metadata - visual object metadata, regarding drawing and image

  • linguistic object metadata - textual and linguistic attributes assigned to an object

docs.title: Searching for a Specific Value
docs.text:
1. If you know the specific record you are looking for, enter it in the dedicated panel located at the top of the interface.

  2. Clicking on an item redirects you to its content, displaying all defined properties.

docs.title: Displaying and Searching Hierarchical Data
docs.text:
Dictionaries structure

Each dictionary is represented by a drop-down list that can be opened by clicking the corresponding link name or by clicking the corresponding dictionary name in the Available Data subsection.

  1. Select a dictionary of interest.

  2. After selecting, an expandable view of the object hierarchy linked to the parent item is displayed (e.g., vessel part).

  3. To display a specific dictionary value, click on the blue "Q" identifier followed by a corresponding number.

docs.title: Manually Adding a New Item
docs.text:
Log in before adding

Adding a new item requires logging in first.

  1. Select the "New item" option from the Main page.

  2. Enter the Label and Description. If aliases exist, they should also be provided here. Complete the process by clicking the "Create" button.

    Language

    Pay close attention to the Language field while adding an item, as an unintentional change may result in incorrect value assignment.

  3. After creating the item, its page will appear on the screen, allowing you to verify the accuracy of the entered data and perform potential edits by clicking the "edit" button.

  4. If the label, description, and aliases are correct, you typically need to define statements pointing to the properties (P) of the item. This is done using the "add statements" button.

  5. To add a new statement, follow steps below:

    • 1 - Enter the appropriate property by its name.

    • 2 - Provide the value representing the given feature.

      Matching types

      Ensure that the added value type matches the property type.

    • 2a (optional) - Add a "reference" indicating the source of the information. Suggested property: described at url (P29).

    • 2b (optional) - Assign a value to the selected property.

      Matching types

      Ensure that the added value type matches the property type.

    • 3 - Save the statement for the item.

  6. After saving the statement, you can assign another value to it ("add value") or create a new statement poining to the item ("add statement").

docs.title: Editing an Existing Item
docs.text:
1. Browse dictionaries for the item of interest (e.g., R'as al Basit).

  2. Click the "edit" button with pencil icon.

    Log in before editing

    Editing an item requires logging in first.

  3. Modify contents and press "save" after completing the change.

  4. Wait for changes to be saved which is indicated by the reappearance of the "edit" button.

docs.title: Deleting an Item
docs.text:
Retrievable Data Loss

This action is not permanent, and the data can be undeleted.

Log in before deleting

Deleting an item requires logging in first.

  1. Browse dictionaries to find the item you want to delete.

  2. (optional) Make sure that the "Tools" pane is displayed on the right side of the selected page. If not, find the "Tools" menu in the upper-right corner of the main content area, expand it, and select the "move to sidebar" option.

  3. In the "Actions" section of the "Tools" pane, select "Delete".

  4. If needed, select a deletion reason from the dropdown menu and provide additional details in the text field (if not, leave the default values). Then, click "Delete page" to remove the item from the Thesaurus.

  5. After deletion, a confirmation message will be displayed.

docs.title: Downloading Content
docs.text:
1. Search dictionary to find items of interest.

  2. Select the checkboxes next to them.

    Note

    To select all values, check the parent item.

  3. Move to the top of the page and click "Download selected as Arches format".

    Note

    As a result, a selected_dictionary_name.rdf file will be downloaded. You can import it to Arches.

docs.title: Thesaurus Management Documentation
docs.text: To access the code repository visit Mare Nostrum LAB GitLab.

docs.title: Browsing Thesaurus
docs.text:
1. Go to the Thesaurus main page.

  2. Click on the desired dictionary (e.g., Provenance).

  3. Navigate to the record of interest (e.g., R'as al-Basit).

    Note

    At this point, you can inspect relations between available items.

  4. Inspect a record of interest by clicking on the internal blue identifier of a subject.

  5. After clicking, Thesaurus opens the site associated with the selected record.

docs.title: Editing Contents
docs.text:
1. Browse Thesaurus to find the desired subject.

  2. Click on the "edit" button with pencil icon.

    Login before editing

    Editing contents requires prior logging in. Further instructions here.

  3. Modify contents and click "save" after completing the change.

  4. Wait for changes to be saved which is indicated by the reappearance of the "edit" button.

    Modifiable elements and non-modifiable elements

    You can modify:

    • Descriptive Label
    • Item Description
    • Aliases/alternative names

    • Labels, Descriptions and Aliases in different languages

      (available: English (EN), Polish (PL), Greek (EL), German (DE), French (FR))

    • Properties of an Item:

      • To modify content of existing property use second ""edit" button with pencil icon.
      • To add new property, select "add statements" with plus icon, choose desired property.

    You cannot modify:

    • Item Identifier (Q followed by a number).

docs.title: Adding New Content
docs.text:
1. Selecting the Target Dictionary

    On the "Main page" in the "Dictionaries" section, there are New [dictionary name] links for creating a new item for each dictionary.

  2. Login and Tool Authorization

    The tool requires authorization, which is initiated via the "Log in to save!" button in the top right corner of the form.

    Note

    You will be redirected to the Mare Nostrum Wiki login page, and then to the OAuth page, where authorization is granted by clicking the "Allow" button at the bottom of the message.

    Note

    OAuth authorization requires prior login.

  3. Filling in Data

    • Labels (required) – the name of the item being added in English

    • Also known as – alternative names for the item

    • Descriptions – a short description of the item to distinguish it from others

    • Subclass of/Part of – the parent element for the item being added

  4. Saving

    Once filled out correctly, the "Create new item" button will appear at the bottom of the page. This initiates saving the item to the database.

    During the save process, a "Creating item..." message will be displayed. Upon successful creation, the "Last items created" section will appear at the bottom of the page with a link to the newly added item.

docs.title: Downloading Content
docs.text:
1. Browse Thesaurus to find items of interest.

  2. Select the checkboxes next to them.

    Note

    To select all values, check the parent item.

  3. Move to the top of the page and click "Download selected as Arches format".

    Note

    As a result, a wikidata_export.rdf file will be downloaded. You can import it to Arches.

docs.title: Context Field Sheet Template
docs.text:
Arches for JU Excavations, together with its Resource Models, has been designed to reflect the excavation recording methodology used by the Jagiellonian University archaeological teams working in Paphos since 2011 within the framework of the Paphos Agora Project.

The system follows the principles of Single Context Recording (SCR), a stratigraphic recording method in which each archaeological context is documented as a separate entity and serves as the fundamental unit of archaeological recording. The structure of the data models, terminology, and relationships implemented in Arches have therefore been developed to correspond with this fieldwork methodology.

The template of the Context Field Sheet currently used for field documentation can be accessed through the links below:

  • Excel version v-2026-09-05: Download PAP Download MAL
  • PDF version v-2026-09-05: Download PAP Download MAL

docs.title: 1. Import Images
docs.text:
Create a directory named with the acquisition date (e.g. 2018_08_04).

Inside this directory, create a project directory named according to the trench and context number, for example:

  • PAP_T_II_154
  • MAL_TT_IV_186_187

Within the project folder:

  • store all photographs intended for photogrammetric processing in an img subdirectory,
  • store additional documentary photographs separately.

docs.title: 2. Save the Project
docs.text:
Save the Metashape project using the following naming convention:

MAL/PAP_trench_context.psx

Example:

PAP_T_VI_520.psx

docs.title: 3. Assess Image Quality
docs.text:
Run: Tools → Estimate Image Quality...

Review a few images with the lowest quality values and identify blurred or problematic photographs.

Show Screenshot Hint

docs.title: 4. Align Images
docs.text:
Run: Workflow → Align Photos...

Recommended settings:

  • Accuracy: High
  • Pair Preselection: Disabled
  • (Advanced) Key point limit: 40 000
  • (Advanced) Tie point limit: 4 000
Show Screenshot Hint

docs.title: 5. Verify Camera Alignment
docs.text:
Inspect the sparse point cloud and camera positions.

Confirm that:

  • camera alignment is correct,
  • image orientation is logical,
  • no misaligned cameras are present.

docs.title: 6. Detect Markers
docs.text:
Run: Tools → Markers → Detect Markers...

Recommended settings:

  • Marker Type: Cross (non-coded)
  • Tolerance: 10 (or higher if necessary)
  • Maximum residual (pix): 3 (or higher if necessary)
Show Screenshot Hint

docs.title: 7. Assign Marker IDs
docs.text:
Review detected markers and assign the correct marker identifiers.

Show Screenshot Hint

docs.title: 8. Import Control Point Coordinates
docs.text: Import the coordinate file containing the surveyed marker coordinates.

docs.title: 9. Complete Missing Marker Measurements
docs.text:
If any markers were not detected automatically, manually place marker projections on the relevant photographs.

Show Screenshot Hint

docs.title: 10. Check Georeferencing Accuracy
docs.text:
Verify the marker residuals and overall georeferencing quality.

A Total Error of approximately 1 cm (0.010 m) or less is generally acceptable for archaeological documentation.

Show Screenshot Hint

docs.title: 11. Generate Point Cloud
docs.text:
Run: Workflow → Build Dense Cloud...

Recommended settings:

  • Quality: Low
  • (Advanced) Depth filtering: Mild
Show Screenshot Hint

docs.title: 12. Inspect the Dense Point Cloud
docs.text:
Check the dense point cloud for:

  • gaps,
  • areas with insufficient coverage,
  • reconstruction artefacts.

docs.title: 13. Define the Reconstruction Region
docs.text:
If necessary, adjust the bounding box using:

Resize Region and Rotate Region

Limit the processing area to the archaeological feature or context being documented.

docs.title: 14. Build the Mesh
docs.text:
Run: Workflow → Build Model...

Recommended settings:

  • Source data: Depth maps
  • Quality: Low
  • Face count: Medium
Show Screenshot Hint

docs.title: 15. Inspect the Mesh
docs.text:
Review the mesh geometry and verify that:

  • the reconstructed surface accurately represents the archaeological context,
  • no significant artefacts are present.

docs.title: 16. Build the Texture
docs.text:
Run: Workflow → Build Texture...

Recommended settings:

  • Texture type: Diffuse map
  • Source data: Images
  • Mapping mode: Generic
  • Blending mode: Mosaic (default)
  • Texture size: 4096
  • Page count: 1
Show Screenshot Hint

docs.title: 17. Verify Texture Quality
docs.text:
Inspect the textured model and check for:

  • blurred areas,
  • texture seams,
  • colour inconsistencies,
  • missing texture coverage.

The project is now ready to be saved for later (automatic) recomputation and export as archaeological documentation.

docs.title: Account Management
docs.text: This section provides information on logging in to the Recogito Studio MN account, resetting an account password, changing profile settings, inviting new users and managing users and their priviledges.

docs.title: Login to Recogito Studio
docs.text:
1. Visit the recogito.mn.cenagis.edu.pl website or click here.

  2. Provide your Username and Password, then click the "Sign In" button.

docs.title: Reset an Account Password
docs.text:
Password reset

To reset a password to the Recogito Studio MN, you must have logged in to the platform at least once and already have an existing account.

  1. Visit the recogito.mn.cenagis.edu.pl website or click here.

  2. Click the "Forgot password?" option.

  3. Provide your email address and submit the reset request.

  4. Wait for the email and follow the instructions provided.

    Check spam folder

    If you do not receive the email, check your spam folder. If there is no message, contact the page administrators.

docs.title: Change Profile Settings
docs.text:
1. Click on your profile icon.

  2. Click "Profile Settings" option.

  3. Provide personal data. For the avatar URL, paste a Web link to the image.

    Note

    It is suggested that the link ends with an image format suffix (e.g., .jpg, .png).

docs.title: Inviting New Users
docs.text:
User priviledges

To invite new users, you need to have Admin organization role.

  1. Click on your profile and go to the "Users" section.

  2. Press the "Invite User" button, provide the email you want to invite to the organization, and send the invitation.

  3. Further information for the invited user is provided in the invitation email.

docs.title: Managing Users and Their Priviledges
docs.text:
User priviledges

To manage users, you need to have Admin organization role.

  1. Click on your profile and go to the "Users" section.

  2. Here, you can inspect information about users, such as First, Last and Display Name, Email, Last Sign In, and User ID. Moreover, you can delete users from the organization and change their Access Level.

docs.title: Appendices
docs.text:
In this section, you can find useful information about:

  • Recogito Studio Roles
  • Annotating TEI Documents with Images
  • Tagging Vocabulary

docs.title: Recogito Studio Roles
docs.text: Recogito natively has two permission levels:

docs.title: Organization Level Roles
docs.text:
1. Org Administrator

    • Can see all projects
    • Can create new projects and add documents to all projects
    • Can browse and annotate documents across all projects
    • Can edit and delete any annotations, document, or entire project
    • Manages users (invites new ones, removes existing ones, changes roles)

  2. Org Professor

    • Can create new projects
    • Does not have access to other people's projects (unless invited)
    • Can add annotations in the projects they belong to

  3. Org Reader

    • By default, only sees projects they are a member of
    • Cannot create their own projects
    • Receives invitations to specific projects

docs.title: Project Level Roles
docs.text:
1. Project Administrator

    • Adds and removes documents within the project
    • Can browse and annotate documents within the project

  2. Project Student

    • Dedicated access for completing tasks within the project

docs.title: Annotating TEI Documents with Images
docs.text: To successfully render images within a TEI text, the document must reference images via accessible Web URLs rather than local paths. If paths are hardcoded, Recogito Studio will fail to load them, preventing the images from displaying.

docs.title: Tagging Vocabulary
docs.text:
You can pre-define a list of tags that will be included in the document by following the steps below:

  1. Open a project, go to the "Documents" tab, and click the "Settings" button.

  2. Go to the "Tagging" tab, provide your list of tags, click "Add to Vocabulary", customize the tags, and save the changes.

docs.title: Main Activities
docs.text:
This section provides information on:

  • creating a new project,
  • adding a new document,
  • modifying document metadata (including Dublin Core),
  • creating a group,
  • annotating TEI texts or PDF documents,
  • annotating IIIF, JPG or PNG images,
  • installing Geotagger plugin in your project,
  • using Geotagger plugin,
  • enabling the Mare Nostrum LAB thesaurus plugin,
  • tagging annotations from the Mare Nostrum LAB thesaurus,
  • creating an assignment,
  • fulfilling an assignment.

docs.title: Create a New Project
docs.text:
User priviledges

To create a new project, you need to have a proper organization role, which means having a Professor or Admin role. Further information can be found here.

  1. Login to Recogito Studio.

  2. Press the "New Project" button in the top right corner of the page.

  3. Provide the project name and description, set projects properties, and press the "Create" button.

    Project properties - Project Visibility

    You can select two options in Project Visibility section:

    • Private - project is visible only to the admin and users who join after receiving an admin invitation.
    • Public - any registered user can access the project by visiting the "Public Projects" section.
    Project properties - Project Type

    You can select two options in Project Type section:

    • Assignments - project admins create assignments with specific documents, and team members fulfil the given tasks.
    • Single Team - project members can annotate any document.

  4. Upon creation, an empty project page will be displayed.

docs.title: Add New Document
docs.text:
1. Create or open a project.

  2. Press the "Add Document" button in the top right corner.

  3. Press the "Import" button and select a file from your device or provide a IIIF manifest.

  4. (Optional) Go to the "All documents" section and select documents of interest from the list of publicly available ones across the organization.

  5. Wait for processing, which ends with a confirmation message and a new document object.

    Note

    To inspect the document from the adding panel, you need to refresh the page by hand.

docs.title: Method 1
docs.text:
1. Open a project, click the three dots in the object representing the document, and click "Edit document metadata".

  2. Add or modify document's metadata and save the changes.

    Note

    Here, you can also change a name of the file in the Recogito Studio.

    Dublin Core

    The metadata form always lists the 15 Dublin Core elements: Contributor, Coverage, Creator, Date, Description, Format, Identifier, Language, Publisher, Relation, Rights, Source, Subject, Title, Type. Empty values are shown as novalue. Extra custom fields can still be added.

docs.title: Method 2
docs.text:
1. Open a project, click the "Add Document" button, and click three vertical dots next to the document of interest.

  2. Here you can edit document metadata (see point 2 in Method 1), change its status, or remove it from Recogito Studio.

    Make Public / Make Private

    This option allows the user to change document accessibility. If status is Private, only users inside a specific project can see this document. If status is Public, any logged-in user can access this file via the "All Documents" section.

docs.title: Create a Project Group
docs.text:
Groups

A Group is a dedicated tool allowing users to thematically aggregate projects (e.g., by source, year, or place).

  1. On the main page, click the "+" button next to the "Groups" section, provide a name, and click the "Create" button.

  2. Go to the created group and add a project. You can select from existing or create a new project that will be assigned to that group.

docs.title: Annotate TEI Texts and PDF Files
docs.text:
Inspect annotations

You can inspect existing annotations by opening a dedicated pane on the right side of the page.

  1. Choose and open a TEI or PDF document.

  2. Mark the pieces of text you want to annotate, provide content for the annotation, and save them.

    Note

    You can add tags to create thematic groups for the annotations.

    Note

    You can add Web URL links, Image URL links and YouTube links to your annotation.

docs.title: Annotate IIIF, JPG and PNG Images
docs.text:
Inspect annotations

You can inspect existing annotations by opening a dedicated pane on the right side of the page.

  1. Choose and open a IIIF, JPG or PNG image.

  2. Select the rectangular or multiangular marking mode, outline the elements of interest, provide annotation contents, and save.

    Note

    You can add tags to create thematic groups for the annotations.

    Note

    You can add Web URL links, Image URL links and YouTube links to your annotation.

docs.title: Install Plugin in Your Project
docs.text:
Plugins availability

Note that plugins are available per project. This means you need to enable them in each project independently.

  1. To enable a plugin, open a project as a Project Admin.

  2. Go to "Settings".

  3. Next, press the "Plugins" tab, click the "Browse Available Plugins" button, and install the listed plugin.

  4. Add gazetteers and save the settings.

    Plugin limitations

    Unfortunatelly, the Core Data gazetteer does not work properly. Including it in your project may cause plugin instabilities.

docs.title: Annotate with Location
docs.text:
1. Install plugin in your project.

  2. Mark the text or part of the image and click the "Add Geo-Tag" button.

  3. Provide a fragment of text. The plugin will automatically match the sentence with the closest tag in the gazetteers. If you are satisfied you can confirm it.

  4. (Optional) If you are not satisfied with the automatic proposition, click "Change", type your text in the dedicated field and choose from displayed list or from the map points.

docs.title: Mare Nostrum LAB thesaurus Plugin
docs.text: This plugin tags annotations with concepts from the Mare Nostrum LAB thesaurus, using the same Recogito plugin shape as Geotagger. It is installed per project.

docs.title: Enable the Plugin in Your Project
docs.text:
Plugins availability

Plugins are available per project. Enable them in each project independently.

  1. Open a project as a Project Admin.

  2. Go to "Settings".

  3. Open the "Plugins" tab, click "Browse Available Plugins", and install Mare Nostrum Lab Thesaurus.

  4. In the plugin settings:

    • choose which dictionaries are searchable,
    • optionally keep Use selected annotation text as the thesaurus search query enabled (on by default).

    Dictionaries include amphora type, vessel form, vessel part, chronology, material, style, and the other MN vocabularies.

docs.title: Annotate with a Thesaurus Tag
docs.text:
1. Enable the plugin in your project.

  2. Mark the text or part of the image, then click "Add Mare Nostrum LAB thesaurus tag".

  3. Type a search string. The plugin queries the thesaurus over SPARQL and lists matching concepts (label, dictionary, description, id).

    Note

    If search-from-selection is on, the selected annotation text is used as the initial query.

  4. Select a concept. The tag is saved on the annotation and links to the item in the thesaurus. You can edit or remove it later from the same annotation.

docs.title: Assignments
docs.text: Assignments can be distributed by the Project Admins to Project Students and assigned with specific tasks.

docs.title: Creating an Assignment
docs.text:
1. While creating a project, select Project Type as Assignments. If you omitted this part, go to project settings and set this variable manually. Remember to save the changes.

  2. (Optional) If you haven't done it yet, go to "Users" and invite the requested group of people as Students.

  3. Switch to the "Assignments" tab and click the "Add Assignment" button. Then, follow the four steps of creation, verify them as a fifth step, and create an assignment.

docs.title: Fulfilling an Assignment
docs.text:
1. (Optional) If you haven't done it yet, join to the project via link, email invitation, or inside Recogito Studio.

  2. Go to "Shared with me" tab and find project you have joined.

    Note

    If you have no assignments, the Project will appear from your perspective.

  3. Open the documents and fulfill the assignments.

docs.title: Recogito

To access the code repository visit Mare Nostrum LAB GitLab.
